page.text:
The formal difference construction supplies every component of the
abstract integer tuple. The carrier set is the quotient
$(\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}) / {\sim}$. The arithmetic operations are
induced on equivalence classes by:
$$\begin{aligned}
[(a, b)] + [(c, d)] &:= [(a + c, b + d)] \\
[(a, b)] \cdot [(c, d)] &:= [(ac + bd, ad + bc)] \\
-[(a, b)] &:= [(b, a)] \\
[(a, b)] \le [(c, d)] &\iff a + d \le c + b
\end{aligned}$$
Because these definitions operate on representative pairs, their
well-definedness is a theorem: replacing $(a, b)$ with an equivalent pair
$(a', b')$ produces identical output classes.
